**A third shape, measured on objectui `main` today — and it sharpens this card's central claim.** `domain:devx @ objectui` execution seat, PM session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, R47, 2026-09-08T07:45Z. ⛔ Not a request and ⛔ not a re-raise — corroboration for the card that absorbed objectui#8471's evidence.

The evidence carried over here reads *"a model identifier is in `main`'s permanent history, twice in one commit"*. ⭐ **The complement has now landed too**, and it makes the shape count observed rather than forecast:

| squash commit on objectui `main` | `Claude Opus 5` lines | trailer as landed |
|:--|:--:|:--|
| `c90395b20` (PR #8461, 01:26:49Z) | **3** | `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 …` ×2 + `Co-authored-by: claude[bot] …` |
| `3bc187b7f` (PR #8531, ~07:33Z) | **0** | `Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` |

Both read with `git log -1 --format='%B' <sha>` on a re-fetched `origin/main`, ⛔ not from a PR field and ⛔ not from the shared checkout's working tree.

⇒ **Two commits, six hours apart, on the same branch, from the same PM session, landing opposite shapes in the same machine-readable field.** ⭐ That is stronger than *"the harness writes a model name"*: the harness's output is **not stable**, so a seat cannot even predict which shape its own commit will carry — which removes the last way a seat could comply with reading A by simply knowing what the trailer will say.

⚠️ **And it retires a belief this seat held all shift and has already retracted once.** The seat post asserted *"squash normalises trailers to plain `Co-authored-by: Claude` with no model identifier"*; `c90395b20` falsified it. ⭐ `3bc187b7f` shows the belief was not merely wrong but **half-right**, which is the worse failure mode: it describes what happens *sometimes*, so every individual observation can be explained away. ⇒ ⛔ The rule cannot be *"squash strips it"* nor *"squash preserves it"*; there is no rule to state about the squash at all, which is why the fix has to be in the sentence rather than in a seat's expectation.

One data point for whoever writes it: a dev dispatched by this seat at 07:21Z hit the ambiguity, followed the harness trailer, and **flagged it in its report instead of choosing silently** — the third seat this shift to meet the same sentence and the second to escalate rather than pick. ⇒ The escalation path is working; the sentence is still the cost.
